topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000000807 (maximal multiplicity of lambda_1 on a flat torus)

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000000277 (maximum Laplace eigenvalue multiplicity on a flat torus)
topic_classifications.reason: Flat-torus Laplace-eigenvalue multiplicities and planar lattice automorphisms; no probability rate function.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000002601 (maximum fixed points of a monotone map on a finite lattice)
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns fixed-point counts of monotone maps on finite order-theoretic lattices. Its lattice terminology is unrelated to arithmetic lattice probability laws; it makes no claim about Cramér rate functions, differentiability, support, variance, or periodic corrections.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000002604 (distributive lattices with equal layer-count vectors)
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns isomorphism of finite distributive lattices from their rank-size vectors. The full body is about order ideals and finite poset counterexamples, not lattice probability distributions or large-deviation rate functions.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000000458 (Möbius number of the Tamari lattice)
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns the Möbius number of the Tamari lattice and a sign/indexing contradiction. No Cramér transform, probability law, differentiability criterion, or lattice correction is discussed.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000000982 (fixed points of the Berezin transform on Fock space)
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns fixed points of the Berezin transform on Gaussian Fock space, harmonic functions, and radiality. Gaussian measure is present, but the claimed result is unrelated to Cramér convex duals or the C2/nonlattice equivalence.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000000418 (proportion of lattice words)
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns lattice/Yamanouchi words, standard tableaux, Kostka numbers, and hook-length counts. Lattice means a word-combinatorics condition, not the support of a probability law; no relevant large-deviation assertion occurs.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000008848 (minimal and maximal fixed points of order-preserving maps)
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns existence and iteration of extremal fixed points of order-preserving maps on posets and complete lattices. Countable/transfinite iteration is unrelated to periodic corrections to a Cramér rate function.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000001556 (chromatic number of a lattice distance graph)
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns chromatic numbers of distance graphs on the spatial lattice Z^2 and periodic colorings. Neither lattice-supported probability laws nor periodic large-deviation corrections are involved.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000002605 (log-concavity of the rank numbers of semimodular lattices)
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns log-concavity of Whitney rank numbers of semimodular order-theoretic lattices, including geometric-lattice/Mason caveats. Log-concavity here is finite combinatorics, with no Cramér rate, support interior, or distributional nonlattice criterion.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000000544
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns toric ideals, integer incidence-kernel lattices, Graver bases, and forest counts. The lattice is an integer kernel, not an arithmetic distribution support; no Cramér or differentiability claim appears.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000001128
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns maximal Schubert-polynomial coefficients and divisibility by a factorial versus a lattice-path count. Both included reviewer/author comments concern an incorrect Schubert polynomial and its correction; none discusses Cramér theory or a lattice probability law.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000001211
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns P-positions of games on Young diagrams under literal poset-game and poison-corner Chomp conventions. Young lattice is an order-theoretic object; no relevant probability, convex dual, support, or smoothness claim occurs.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000002160
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns the Higman–Sims graph independence number versus its Hoffman spectral bound. The Delsarte-semilattice clause is expressly outside scope; neither clause concerns Cramér rate functions.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000000277
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns Laplacian eigenvalue multiplicities of the square lattice torus, obtained from integer vectors of a fixed squared norm. Spatial/dual lattices and spectral multiplicity have no substantive overlap with the Cramér C2/nonlattice criterion.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000001128 (v3: correct Schubert polynomial)
topic_classifications.reason: Corrected submission about the Schubert-polynomial factorial divisibility counterexample from PR161. Its sole reviewer comment requests a faithful divided-difference construction; no probability law or Cramér functional is discussed.

topic_classifications.title: Prove conjecture 00000002486: the dominance order on partitions of n is a self-dual lattice
topic_classifications.reason: Proves the dominance lattice and conjugation duality of integer partitions. The body mentions a Legendre-type duality between finite partial sums and positive-part sums, but does not concern a log-mgf, Cramér rate function, C2 regularity, or lattice distributions.

topic_classifications.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000001464
topic_classifications.reason: Concerns impossibility of a convex function with genuine period three under iterated Legendre transformation, using involutivity/Fenchel–Moreau. Although Legendre duality and periodicity are shared words, the period is iteration of the transform, not a periodic lattice correction; there is no Cramér/log-mgf or nonlattice differentiability assertion.
